text:
jules: Heads-up — saw a reproducible tail-latency spike during last night's canary that only shows up when we have sticky KV leases + long-running LLM sessions. p95 doubled for ~7% of requests.
jules: Root cause looks like lease staleness: requests still routed to drained/evicted hosts while their KV prefix wasn't warmed -> heavy KV misses + disk swap.
karen: ugh. was that the cohort that had session affinity pinned?
jules: yep. small cohort (5% traffic) with long chat sessions (~20-30min), lots of prefix reuse. when a host entered graceful-drain the new host didn't have KV so micro-backpressure cascaded.
mike: Are we sure it's routing vs auth/timeout? logs show route decisions at proxy, then a 30–50ms spike at model server which matches KV miss + load.
elaine: Can we mitigate with a hedging/fallback policy rather than full rollback? rollback is costly for product continuity.
jules: thinking: introduce "soft-evict" + probe multiplier. Instead of immediate cutover, route X% of session requests to new host and probe KV warmup. When probe success-rate > threshold promote. If p95_new / p95_old > 1.5 -> fallback.
karen: sounds like we need a deterministic fallback trigger. what signals do we use? p95, error-rate, probe-failure-rate, queue-depth?
mike: prefer a small set: p95 delta, probe-miss-rate, and a smoothed CPU/queue signal. Keep decisions local to routing plane to avoid coordination overhead.
jules: agree. proposal for decision logic (pseudo-config):
```json
{"policy":"soft-evict","probe_ratio":0.1,"probe_window_s":60,"p95_delta_threshold":1.5,"probe_success_threshold":0.8,"max_probe_backoff_s":300}
```
elaine: Nice. How will we treat session affinity? if session still pinned to old host, do we split affinity or migrate?
jules: option A: sticky-split -> pin new requests to new host, continue serving affinity on old until session end. Option B: migratory-swap -> actively migrate KV prefixes during switchover (more complex but faster).
karen: For safety and lower complexity start with sticky-split. Migration can be future work.
mike: We should also add an escape hatch: global cutover if aggregate p95 >= x OR error-rate spikes for >N minutes. infra-bot: @deploy-bot would emit these metrics as events so rollout controller can stop.
elaine: operationally, need visibility in Console: per-cohort probe success, probe-ratio, current soft-evict state, and last fallback reason.
jules: yes — add telemetry hooks: route decisions, per-probe result, TTL of KV prefix, and sampled request traces. Keep retention short for cost.
karen: any perf cost of probing? 10% probe_ratio seems high for small cohorts. maybe start at 2% and ramp with probe_success.
mike: agree. implement exponential backoff on probe_ratio: 2% -> 5% -> 10% on successes. cap at configured max.
jules: implementation notes: 1) small state machine in routing plane per-variant cohort, 2) probe handler that can warm KV via async prefetch RPC, 3) metric sampler, 4) fallback controller that can change weights.
elaine: testing plan? canary smoke, then degraded traffic with synthetics that hit long-session paths. record p50/p95/p99 and KV-miss fraction.
karen: add a chaos test where we inject delayed KV loads on the target to ensure fallback triggers.
mike: I'll sketch the RFC draft and a simple simulator to tune thresholds. leaning toward local decisions with a central override.
jules: thanks — if folks OK I'll open the RFC + a short runbook for oncall. probably ping eng-oncall for the first 48h after rollout. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: scheduled-canary: canary job 2024-04-09T02:00Z created for variant v3, notify eng-infra on any route-level fallback events.
elaine: perfect. I'll add Console panels and a quick alert rule for probe-failure > 0.2 over 5m.
mike: ping me if you want help building the simulator.
jules: closing loop: I'll draft RFC by EOD, include config examples and the runbook. thanks all.
